title: Optimized proximity ligation assay (PLA) for detection of RNA-protein complex interactions in cell lines
protocol: Seed 1 × 10^4 HeyA8 cells per well of 24-well plate in 1 mL of culture medium per well for transfection.
Incubate the seeded cells overnight.
Prepare 2 nM 6-FAM-labeled oligonucleotides by adding to 100 μL Opti-MEM medium.
Dilute lipofectamine 2000 at a concentration of 2.5 μl in 100 μL Opti-MEM medium.
Incubate both solutions at 20°C–25°C for 5 minutes.
Mix the oligonucleotide solution with the lipofectamine solution.
Incubate the mixture at 20°C–25°C for 20 minutes.
Add the transfection mixture to the cells.
Replace the transfection reagent containing medium with regular culture medium after 4 hours.
Trypsinize cells 24 hours after transfection.
Count cells for density using an automated cell counter or hemocytometer.
Resuspend cells to a density of 1 × 10^3 cells in 1,200 μL of growth media.
Add 100 μL equally into the wells of 12-well glass bottom chamber slides.
Allow cells to attach on glass bottom for 5 minutes under the hood.
Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Transfect HeyA8 cells with 5 nM pre-designed siRNAs for human MYC using Lipofectamine RNAiMAX according to manufacturer instructions.
After 48 hours, transfect cells again with 5′FAM-labeled oligonucleotides.
Ensure that the cells are in a healthy state, properly mixed, and evenly distributed into the wells.
Check the suspended cells before incubation at 37°C to ensure they are homogeneously distributed without aggregation.
Aspirate off media from the cells.
Wash with 1× DPBS.
Fix the cells with 4% PFA in PBS for 20 min at 25°C.
Gently discard the fixative solution.
Wash with 1× DPBS.
Add 100 μL of ice-cold methanol or acetone to cells.
Incubate at −20°C for 15–30 min to permeabilize.
Gently discard the methanol solution.
Wash the cells two times with 1× DPBS gently.
Add 50 μL of blocking solution on chambers glass slide.
Incubate for 1 h at 4°C in a humidified chamber.
Heat specific biotin labeled oligonucleotide probes at 70°C for 3 min.
Put the heated probes immediately on ice.
Add 30 μL of the probes to each well of a chamber glass slide.
Incubate for 1 h at 37°C or alternatively overnight at 4°C in a humidified chamber.
Heat probes at 70°C for 3 minutes.
Immediately cool probes in an ice-water bath.
Incubate primary antibodies biotin (anti-mouse) and FXR1 (anti-rabbit) overnight in a 1:100 ratio diluted in 1× antibody diluent.
Perform positive and negative controls for PLA assay in advance.
Incubate samples with biotin antibody alone or FXR1 antibody alone as primary antibodies followed by proximity ligation probe hybridization with PLA probes.
Use PLA probe Anti-Rabbit Plus and PLA probe Anti-Mouse Plus for FXR1 detection to determine suitability of primary antibody for PLA assay.
Employ two PLA probes Anti-Mouse Plus for biotin and Anti-Rabbit Plus for FXR1 as negative control to identify non-specific background signals.
Conduct no primary antibodies and no PLA probes controls to confirm specificity of antibodies and PLA probes.
Add a solution of 1× PBS in each well without removing the blocking solution.
Gently aspirate with vacuum pump immediately.
Add 30 μL of the corresponding primary antibodies solution in the chamber slide.
Incubate overnight at 4°C in a humidified chamber.
Fill with 1× PBS in non-used wells of the chamber slides.
Add Wash Buffer A in each well.
Incubate on a shaker at slow speed (10–30 × g) for 5 min.
Remove the wash buffer with vacuum pump and repeat this step twice.
Dilute the two PLA probes Anti-Mouse Plus and Anti-Rabbit Plus stock solutions in antibody diluent to a 1:5 ratio.
Add 30 μL of the diluted PLA probe solution on the chamber slide.
Incubate for 1 hour at 37°C.
Add Wash Buffer A into each well.
Incubate on a shaker at low speed.
Remove the wash buffer using a vacuum pump and repeat this step twice.
Prepare the ligation reaction solution between the second and third washing steps at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Gently remove the wash buffer A with a vacuum pump after the second wash.
Add 30 μL of the prepared ligation reaction mix on the cover glass.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 37°C.
Add Wash Buffer A into each well.
Incubate on a shaker at low speed.
Remove the wash buffer using a vacuum pump and repeat this step twice.
Prepare the rolling cycle amplification solution during the washing steps, ensuring it is protected from light and maintained at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Add Wash Buffer A into each well for the final wash after ligation incubation.
Incubate on a shaker at low speed.
Remove the wash buffer using a vacuum pump and repeat this step twice.
Gently remove wash buffer A with a vacuum pump after the second time.
Add 30 μL of amplification reaction mix in the chamber slide.
Incubate for 1.5 h at 37°C in the dark.
Add wash Buffer B in each well.
Incubate on a shaker at low speed.
Remove wash buffer with a vacuum pump and repeat this step twice.
Gently remove wash buffer B with a vacuum pump.
Add 100 μL of 0.01× wash buffer B diluted in high purity water.
Air-dry for 2 min.
Add 50 μL of PLA mounting medium on glass slide.
Alternatively, add 50 μL of mounting medium with DAPI on glass slide.
Put the cover slip over the slide slowly using forceps.
Avoid producing air bubbles during the process.
Seal the edges of the cover slip with nail polish if not using ProLong Glass Antifade Mountant.
Store the slide at 4°C before processing to microscopy image acquisition.
Do not freeze the slide, as freezing will create large crystal particles in the mounting medium.
Scan images at a 20× lens first to locate cells on the slide.
Switch to a 40× lens for detailed imaging after locating cells.
Capture and save at least three images for each group for further analysis.
Scan images using a 20× lens initially for a general view and cell identification.
Process image acquisition starting with DAPI channel (450 nm).
Proceed to FAM channel (488 nm) for imaging.
Continue with Cy3 channel (545 nm) for imaging.
Optimize filters if different fluorescent tags are used.
Use 488 nm/527 nm filter for green fluorescence detection.
Apply 554 nm/576 nm filter for Cy3 orange fluorescence detection.
Utilize 644 nm/670 nm filter for Cy5 far red fluorescence detection.
Ensure all slides from the same experiment are imaged under identical conditions.
Use water on lens at 40× magnification and keep slides facing glass cover on bottom.
Check unstained well of slide to confirm presence or absence of autofluorescence.
Open a TIFF image in ImageJ software.
Go to Process/Binary/Make Binary to convert the TIFF images into binary format.
Select region of interest representing only one cell using the selection tool from the main menu.
Select Process/Filter/Median 2.0.
Click the main menu again and select Process/Binary/Watershed to segment spots.
In the main menu, select Process/Find Maxima to exclude edge maxima and light background.
Choose “Count” in the output type for automatic calculation of PLA spots presented as mean ± standard deviation for three different images.
Select “Point section” in the output type to mark each PLA spot with yellow crosses from a single cell.
Open a high magnification TIFF image in ImageJ software.
Split the image into individual images displaying MYC (green), PLA dots (red), and DAPI using the Image/Color/Split image option.
Save the individual images.
Select Plugin/JAcoP in the main menu of ImageJ.
Choose Red channel for PLA dots and Green channel for MYC protein analysis.
Save the selected images.
Go to the Analysis tab in the main menu.
Select Overlap and Manders’ coefficients as parameters.
Adjust signal thresholds for channel A and B to avoid background interference and signal saturation.
Click analyze.
Record Manders’ coefficients and Overlap coefficient from the data window.
Plot the recorded data in a table or graph format.
Perform statistical analysis using quantitated values.
